title: Royal Air Force NS11 crash
summary: RAF airship NS11 took off from RNAS Pulham around midnight on 14/15 July 1919 on a mine-hunting patrol over the North Sea. She flew beneath a long greasy black cloud off Cley. Locals reported an abnormal noise from her engines. She was returning towards the coast when she exploded into a ball of flames with a second explosion as she descended into the sea. All nine crew members perished. The official Court of Enquiry findings were inconclusive but lightning strike was considered a possibility.
probable_cause: Possible lightning strike or engine-related cause, but findings inconclusive

title: Wingfoot Air Express crash

location.name: Chicago Loop, Illinois Trust and Savings Building

summary: The Wingfoot Air Express, a Goodyear FD hydrogen-filled airship, caught fire and crashed into the Illinois Trust and Savings Bank building in Chicago. The hydrogen ignited at 1200 feet altitude over the Chicago Loop. Two crew parachuted safely and one died when his parachute caught fire; the airship's flaming debris fell through the bank's skylight, killing 10 bank employees.
probable_cause: Hydrogen caught fire for unknown reasons
